value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\left(1\right)y=6,\quad y(0)=-6
$$

Select the correct options below.

The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}."] [:db/add "2be7fd07-ba52-508f-89b0-10b9de9cd5dc" :question/worked-solution "This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x),
$$

with $P(x)=1$ and $Q(x)=6.$

We compute an integrating factor using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 1\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)=e^{x}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+1y) & =e^{x}\cdot 6 \\ e^{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+e^{x}y & =6 e^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x}) & =6 e^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 6 e^{x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{x} & =6\left(1 e^{x}\right)+C \\ ye^{x} & =6 e^{x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 6 e^{x}\right) e^{- x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(6 e^{(0)})+C}{(e^{(0)})} \\ -6 & =\frac{6+C}{1} \\ C & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=6 - 12 e^{- x}.
$$"] [:db/add "2be7fd07-ba52-508f-89b0-10b9de9cd5dc" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "2be7fd07-ba52-508f-89b0-10b9de9cd5dc" :question/answer-fields $$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x),
$$

with $P(x)=1$ and $Q(x)=5.$

We compute an integrating factor using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 1\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)=e^{x}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+1y) & =e^{x}\cdot 5 \\ e^{x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+e^{x}y & =5 e^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x}) & =5 e^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 5 e^{x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{x} & =5\left(1 e^{x}\right)+C \\ ye^{x} & =5 e^{x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 5 e^{x}\right) e^{- x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(5 e^{(0)})+C}{(e^{(0)})} \\ 6 & =\frac{5+C}{1} \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{3 x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 18 e^{3 x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{3 x} & =18\left(\frac{1}{3} e^{3 x}\right)+C \\ ye^{3 x} & =6 e^{3 x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 6 e^{3 x}\right) e^{- 3 x}\end{aligned}

\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x),

with $P(x)=4$ and $Q(x)=16.$

We compute an integrating factor using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 4\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{4 x}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{4 x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y) & =e^{4 x}\cdot 16 \\ e^{4 x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4 e^{4 x}y & =16 e^{4 x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{4 x}) & =16 e^{4 x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{4 x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 16 e^{4 x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{4 x} & =16\left(\frac{1}{4} e^{4 x}\right)+C \\ ye^{4 x} & =4 e^{4 x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 4 e^{4 x}\right) e^{- 4 x}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(4 e^{4 (0)})+C}{(e^{4 (0)})} \\ -1 & =\frac{4+C}{1} \\ C & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{3 x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 18 e^{3 x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{3 x} & =18\left(\frac{1}{3} e^{3 x}\right)+C \\ ye^{3 x} & =6 e^{3 x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 6 e^{3 x}\right) e^{- 3 x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=4$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(6 e^{3 (0)})+C}{(e^{3 (0)})} \\ 4 & =\frac{6+C}{1} \\ C & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=6 - 2 e^{- 3 x}.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Solving First-Order Initial Value Problems Using Integrating Factors

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\left(4\right)y=16,\quad y(0)=-1
$$

Select the correct options below.

An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x),
$$

with $P(x)=4$ and $Q(x)=16.$

We compute an integrating factor using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{\int 4\,\text{d}x} \\  & =e^{4 x}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)=e^{4 x}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{4 x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y) & =e^{4 x}\cdot 16 \\ e^{4 x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4 e^{4 x}y & =16 e^{4 x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{4 x}) & =16 e^{4 x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ye^{4 x})\,\text{d}x & =\int 16 e^{4 x}\,\text{d}x \\ ye^{4 x} & =16\left(\frac{1}{4} e^{4 x}\right)+C \\ ye^{4 x} & =4 e^{4 x}+C \\ y & =\left(C + 4 e^{4 x}\right) e^{- 4 x}\end{aligned}
$$

This is the general solution. To find the value of $C$ corresponding to the specific solution, we apply the initial condition $y(0)=-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =\frac{(4 e^{4 (0)})+C}{(e^{4 (0)})} \\ -1 & =\frac{4+C}{1} \\ C & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=4 - 5 e^{- 4 x}.
$$
